title: MySQL: Add suport for semisync
description:
Semisync is an enhancement for the replication protocol of MySQL. This allows the server to request acknowledgements of binlog events. This is to make sure an `INSERT` only returns OK on the primary if n (default = 1) replicas have received the event.

If this is enabled there is a marker 0xef and a flag (0x0 ack not expected - or - 0x1 ack expected) added before events send to the replicas. (total 2 bytes).

Then replicas send an ACK event back, also with a 0xef marker. These events have a position (8 byte) and a file name (not length encoded, not NUL terminated, just until the end of the packet).

Note that the 0xef is not a command like COM_QUERY nor a binlog event type like FORMAT_DESCRIPTION_EVENT.

- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/replication-semisync.html
- https://jan.kneschke.de/projects/mysql/mysql-55s-semi-sync-replication-the-protocol-side/
- https://mariadb.com/kb/en/4-semi-sync-replication/

Capture, recommended to filter on `tcp.stream eq 0 && mysql`. Use `Decode as...` to decode traffic on port 3308 as mysql.
[semisync.pcapng.gz](/uploads/9795eda571e007762aceb5c04e8ded44/semisync.pcapng.gz)
